runtimes.notes: Default server port changed from 8080 to 9931 on 2026-10-09 (PR #30159, first nightly b11521). The llama.app installer and winget currently ship b11540, which listens on 9931 (tested). Homebrew stable 0.6.0 still listens on 8080 and prints 'notice: server default port will be changed to :9931 in a future release'. The llama.app docs pages (quickstart, serve) still say 8080. The server prints 'listening on http://127.0.0.1:PORT'; tell users to open that URL, or pin it with --port. Without :{quant}, -hf picks Q4_K_M, then Q8_0, then the first GGUF in the repo (common/download.cpp); ggml-org repos often have only Q4_0/Q8_0/BF16, so ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF resolves to Q8_0 (834 MB). Since 0.6.x, -hf downloads go to the standard Hugging Face cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub, or LLAMA_CACHE / HF_HUB_CACHE / HF_HOME), not ~/Library/Caches/llama.cpp. The unified `llama` binary also has `llama bench`. The llama.app install.sh only has prebuilt Mac binaries for brand strings M1-M5 and A18 (Metal), so Intel Macs get 'No prebuilt llama binary is available' and should use Homebrew. The web UI is served gzip-only: curl without --compressed gets 415, but browsers are fine.
runtimes.vision: -hf downloads the matching mmproj automatically, choosing the closest quant (Q8_0 mmproj for a Q4_K_M model). Disable it with --no-mmproj. Tested with SmolVLM2: modalities text, vision, video.
runtimes.split: Split GGUFs (-00001-of-0000N), including ones in a per-quant subfolder, are resolved by {repo}:{quant}, and every shard is downloaded. Tested.

runtimes.notes: Write `lms get` with the full https://huggingface.co/ URL. A bare `lms get {repo}@{quant}` is looked up as an LM Studio Hub artifact and fails: 'Failed to resolve artifact "unsloth/qwen3-0.6b-gguf": The artifact does not exist or you do not have permission to read it'. The quant goes after @ (case-insensitive). After the download, lms names the model by a derived key (e.g. qwen3-0.6b), not the repo id, and `lms load mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit` fails with 'No model found that matches model key'. A GGUF and an MLX build of one model can share the same key. `lms chat -p` with no model loaded gives 'No loaded model found, load with: lms load'. If the app is not running, lms starts it as a background service (--run-as-service). On first launch the app appended `export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.lmstudio/bin"` to ~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile and ~/.profile. Models are stored in ~/.lmstudio/models/{owner}/{repo}/. The server is OpenAI-compatible at http://localhost:1234/v1. LM Studio has no `lms rm`; delete models in the app's My Models view or remove the folder. macOS needs Apple Silicon and macOS 14+; Intel Macs are not supported. The deep link format comes from Hugging Face's 'Use this model' button definition (huggingface.js local-apps.ts), not from LM Studio's own docs, which only document lmstudio://add_mcp.
runtimes.vision: lms get downloads the mmproj automatically (it chose mmproj-...-f16.gguf for SmolVLM2 Q4_K_M), and `lms ls --json` shows vision: true. An image sent to /v1/chat/completions was answered correctly (tested).

runtimes.notes: From HF docs: 'ollama run hf.co/{username}/{repository}:{quantization}'; the quant is case-insensitive and a full .gguf file name also works. Without a tag, HF's registry chooses: Q4_K_M if present, otherwise 'one reasonable quant type'. For ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF, which has no Q4_K_M, that was the 1.56 GB BF16, so always pass :{quant}. Split/sharded repos are rejected (HTTP 400, tested). 11434 is an API, not a web page; the OpenAI-compatible base is http://localhost:11434/v1. Tested on Ollama 0.30.8, the version installed here; the latest is 0.40.2 (2026-10-08) and was not installed. Library tags confirmed to exist on registry.ollama.ai: llama3.2:3b, qwen3.5:4b, qwen3.5:0.8b, gemma3:270m, qwen3:0.6b, gemma4:latest.

The one-shot CLI form with an image path printed 'Added image' but then an empty reply for SmolVLM2. That looks model- or template-specific and was not investigated further.
runtimes.split: Not supported. The registry answers: 'This repository only contains sharded GGUF files. Ollama does not yet support pulling sharded GGUF via the registry; please download the shards and merge them locally with `ollama create` (workaround detailed at https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/5245), or use a repository with single-file quantizations.'

runtimes.notes: API only, with no web UI (GET / returns 404). The server listens on http://localhost:8080/v1 by default ('This will start a text generation server on port `8080`'), which is the same default port as Homebrew llama.cpp 0.6.0. Hugging Face's 'Use this model' snippet curls localhost:8000, which is wrong for mlx_lm.server. Needs Python >= 3.11 (PyPI) and Apple silicon. Downloads use the Hugging Face cache. huggingface_hub 2.2.0 (pulled in by mlx-lm 0.32.0) now writes into a shared ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/blobs store, so deleting a models--* folder does not free the space.
